claims.text: Oxidation degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is primarily governed by the kinetics of Cr2O3 scale formation.
A uniform Cr distribution in the as-printed alloy rapidly forms a continuous protective Cr2O3 barrier.
Precipitation aging produces Cr-depleted L12 and L21 nanoprecipitates.
The Cr-depleted precipitates delay or disrupt formation of a continuous Cr2O3 layer.
Precipitate–matrix interfaces provide additional oxygen-diffusion pathways, particularly at higher temperatures.
The additional oxygen-diffusion pathways cause the aged alloy to have greater oxidation mass gain.
The as-printed SLM alloy is more than 97% dense.
The as-printed alloy has a single-fcc cellular microstructure with dislocation-rich cell walls and a uniform Cr distribution.
Aging at 750°C for 50 h induces approximately 25–30 vol% Ni/Ti-enriched nanoscale L12 precipitates.
Aging at 750°C for 50 h induces larger Al/Ti-enriched and Cr/Fe-depleted L21 precipitates.
The proposed comparison exposes as-printed and aged samples at 600, 750, 900, 1050, and 1200°C for up to 96 h.
The oxide scale develops from a duplex structure into a trilayer consisting of an outer mixed or spinel oxide, a continuous Cr-rich intermediate layer, and a discontinuous inner Al/Ti-rich region.
All alloying elements initially form loose or discontinuous surface oxides.
Cr diffuses rapidly because of its smaller atomic size and favorable mobility.
A dense Cr2O3 barrier limits subsequent oxidation in the as-printed alloy.
The protective role of the Cr2O3 scale is most effective up to approximately 900°C.
Above approximately 900°C, scale defects associated with precipitate–matrix interfaces increase oxidation rates.
Exposure for up to 96 h reveals a transition from subparabolic to nearly parabolic oxidation behavior.
The aged alloy will have higher mass gain and thicker oxide scales than the as-printed alloy, especially above 900°C, while both states retain similar oxide-growth activation energies.
The aging-induced oxidation changes will not significantly compromise strength or fatigue performance.
